# THEORYs with `tags` `learning-theory`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Learning theory** — why learning generalizes and how it proceeds — compression and description length, Kolmogorov complexity and sufficient statistics, rate–distortion and PAC-style bounds, model selection; and training dynamics: solvable models of learning trajectories, stages, plateaus and phase transitions in training, and the implicit bias of optimisation. A work whose subject is how to train a model better is ML practice and goes to the anthology (ADR-036).

| [THEORY-030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md) v3 | For a memory evolving reversibly with its environment, Landauer's bound prices only steps that lose logical distinguishability, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit lost, exported to the environment and not necessarily as heat, so copying onto a blank register, measuring or evaluating a bit has no minimum cost; learning a label has a floor only in total entropy production, at least the information learnt, which in Goldt and Seifert's perceptron can be paid in the weights' own entropy with vanishing heat | Bennett (2003), [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md): the cost attaches to many-to-one maps of the logical state, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit exported to non-information-bearing degrees of freedom, which "need not" be heat. Goldt & Seifert ([LIT-308](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-308.md)) bound information learnt by total entropy production, payable with vanishing heat in their toy model. It does not license a k_BT ln 2 heat floor per judgment, per gradient step or per bit learnt. Whether the bound survives without reversible dynamics is [QUESTION-215](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-215.md). | Active |

| [THEORY-078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md) v2 | The top C eigenvalues of a trained C-class classifier's Fisher are carried by the second moment of its class-mean logit derivatives, so a cut at the bulk edge keeps the span of the class means, and they stand clear of the bulk to the extent between-class separation exceeds within-class variation | Papyan (2019), [LIT-619](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-619.md): for softmax cross-entropy the Gauss–Newton matrix G, which is the model's Fisher averaged over inputs, is an uncentred second moment of logit derivatives indexed by class and logit. Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md), splits those C into one global-mean outlier and C − 1 between-class ones, finds a C(C − 1) cross-class mini-bulk beneath them, and proves the whole pattern for a Gaussian toy model. | [THEORY-079](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-079.md) v2 | Bayesian model reduction under the Laplace approximation prices the reductions of a singular parent model with a Gaussian Occam factor, so its free-energy differences can be wrong by a term that grows with log n | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. BMR's closed form (Friston & Penny, [LIT-620](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-620.md), Eq. 9; Friston, Parr & Zeidman, [LIT-614](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-614.md), Eq. 11) charges a reduction through log-determinants of Gaussian precisions, which is MacKay's regular Occam factor. Watanabe, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), says that models with hierarchical layers or hidden variables are singular, that no normal distribution approximates their posterior, and that their free energy grows as λ log n. BMR is applied to exactly such models: mixtures, hierarchical empirical Bayes and latent states. Neither literature cites the other. The exact identity is untouched ([THEORY-081](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-081.md)). The claim is about its Laplace form, and a test on reduced-rank regression would settle it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-080](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-080.md) v3 | In a linearised network with a Gaussian prior on its parameters, the Occam factor is a sum over the NTK's eigenvalues, so on spherical data each harmonic pays ½ log(1 + βnµ_k/α) and the kernel's eigenvalue decay schedules the complexity penalty across frequencies | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. Its exact half is filed as the record's own claim, CLAIM-384; what stays here is the spherical account. A network linearised at initialisation, with an isotropic Gaussian prior on its parameters and Gaussian noise, is MacKay's linear-in-parameters model ([LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md)). Its Occam factor is −½ Σ log(1 + βλ_a/α) over the eigenvalues of JᵀJ. These are the empirical NTK's, which on uniform spherical data form Bietti & Bach's degree blocks, nµ_k with multiplicity N(d, k) ([LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md)). Degrees whose βnµ_k exceeds α pay about ½ log n per harmonic, and degrees below pay almost nothing. With µ_k ~ k^(−d), the number of paid directions γ grows as n^((d−1)/d), not as the parameter count. Basri et al.'s bound ([LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md), Eq. 14) is the matching data-fit term. The kernel's decay exponent is the schedule of the penalty. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-082](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-082.md) | Steepest descent is defined only relative to a metric, and Amari's proof that natural-gradient learning is Fisher efficient needs the Fisher information at the optimum to be invertible, the condition whose failure WBIC calls singular; in a multilayer perceptron it fails wherever an output weight is zero | Amari (1998), [LIT-607](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-607.md). Theorem 1 is a Lagrangian derivation: under \|dw\|² = Σg_ij dw_i dw_j the steepest-descent direction is −G⁻¹∇L, so it changes with G. Theorem 2 shows that online learning with step 1/t along the Fisher natural gradient attains the Cramér–Rao bound G⁻¹/t, and its proof uses G(w*)⁻¹. Watanabe, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), Eq. 14, calls a truth regular when the optimum is one point and its Fisher is positive definite, and singular otherwise. From Amari's own Eq. 6.12, the score for hidden unit i's input weights carries the factor v_i. So the Fisher of a multilayer perceptron loses rank wherever an output weight is zero. That set is part of the optimum whenever the teacher needs fewer hidden units than the student has. Active because each step is checkable in the two texts. The claim that the Fisher is the only invariant metric is Chentsov's, cited and not held. | Active |
| [THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md) v3 | In Papyan, Han and Donoho's runs of VGG, ResNet and DenseNet trained with cross-entropy on seven balanced datasets without augmentation, training past zero error shrinks last-layer within-class variability against between-class variability, and moves the centred class means and the classifier toward a common simplex equiangular tight frame and the decision toward nearest class mean, nearly to completion on the four easier datasets and only partly on ImageNet | Papyan, Han & Donoho (2020), [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md), measured 480 trained classifiers on seven datasets with VGG, ResNet and DenseNet. Through the terminal phase, within-class variability of last-layer features falls (NC1), and the centred class means become equinorm and equiangular with cosine −1/(C − 1) (NC2). The classifier aligns with them (NC3), and the decision becomes nearest class mean (NC4). They prove that NC1 and NC2 imply NC3 and NC4 for the MSE-optimal and max-margin classifiers, and that the simplex ETF is the unique error-exponent-optimal codebook. Read from the plots, collapse is close to complete on the four easier datasets and partial on ImageNet at the last epoch. Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md), sees class means separate and grow more orthogonal with depth. The measurements cover one protocol, and the dynamics are unexplained outside free-features models. Within them, THEORY-278 (LIT-974) derives collapse for MSE under a re-whitened flow, and THEORY-286 (LIT-994) gives the cross-entropy endpoint under class imbalance. | [THEORY-195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md) v3 | On the Random Hierarchy Model, in the experiments reported (s = 2, L ≤ 4, small v), deep CNNs matched to the tree and trained in a feature-learning regime reach a tenth of chance error from about n_c m^L examples, polynomial in the input dimension, at the training-set size at which their hidden layers become invariant to swapping synonymous tuples; two-layer networks and the same CNNs as fixed kernels need a number proportional to the whole input space, exponential in the input dimension, and deep CNNs stay near chance when every tuple is made equally likely in every class | Cagnetta, Petrini, Tomasini, Favero and Wyart (2023), [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md): measured for depth-(L + 1) CNNs and deep fully connected networks on the Random Hierarchy Model with s = 2 and L ≤ 4, with a large-v scaling argument for the correlation threshold and an exact one-step-gradient model of a two-layer network on one patch. | [THEORY-206](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-206.md) v2 | For networks of smooth units without biases, one hidden layer needs exactly ∏(rᵢ+1) neurons to match the monomial x₁^r₁⋯xₙ^rₙ's Taylor polynomial at the origin, and a deep network O(Σ log rᵢ), with the upper bounds holding for uniform approximation too, so the cost of flattening a polynomial grows exponentially with its degree in distinct variables and not with the number of inputs: products of many inputs separate depths, bounded-degree polynomials do not | Rolnick and Tegmark (2017), [LIT-890](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-890.md), Theorems 4.1 to 4.3, extending Lin, Tegmark and Rolnick's 2ⁿ for a product ([LIT-887](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-887.md)). | [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md) v2 | A converged network trained with SGD is not at a point and does not sample its training loss: under a quadratic approximation it samples a Gibbs distribution on a modified loss, isotropic in the Hessian's column space, with probability currents that keep it oscillating, so its speed and spread are set by the learning rate, momentum and batch size | Kunin et al. (2021), [LIT-1011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1011.md), read in [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md). | [THEORY-210](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-210.md) v2 | Continuous parameter symmetries stretch a network's minima into connected manifolds along which the loss is flat, and give gradient flow conserved quantities that fix where on such a manifold training ends; finite steps, gradient noise and weight decay break them, so the position along a symmetry orbit is set by initialization and optimizer, not by the loss | Zhao, Walters & Yu (2025), [LIT-970](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-970.md), read in [NOTE-712](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-712.md): a survey, so the dynamical results are secondhand. Read first-hand (Neural Mechanics; Ziyin et al.), weight decay drives the conserved quantities toward zero, and minibatch noise drives a rescaling symmetry's toward the point where the layers' gradient noise balances. In a diagonal linear network the stationary distribution follows exactly: it is non-ergodic, has a memory of initialization, and collapses to zero above a critical temperature. | [THEORY-278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-278.md) v3 | Under MSE loss, in Han, Papyan and Donoho's VGG, ResNet and DenseNet runs on five balanced ten-class datasets, the trained classifier stays near the least-squares classifier for its own features from an early epoch; and on that central path, for unconstrained features continually renormalized to identity within-class covariance and without weight decay, gradient flow drives the class-separation singular values to infinity at equal rates, which in that model is neural collapse | Han, Papyan & Donoho (2021), [LIT-974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-974.md), read in [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md). Under a flow that re-whitens the features after every step, each ω_j grows as (4t/N)^(1/4), and their ratios tend to 1. That is NC1 and NC2, and NC3–NC4 follow. | [THEORY-279](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-279.md) v2 | Early in training, image classifiers and language models act on the low-order statistics of their inputs, first-order before second-order, and later lose that sensitivity as they come to use higher-order structure | Belrose et al. | [THEORY-283](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-283.md) v2 | For a hierarchical multi-index target with isotropic Gaussian inputs and even, separable links, direction k becomes weakly recoverable by the Bayes-optimal estimator at a sample count proportional to its squared weight to the power minus one, so features emerge one at a time through sharp spectral transitions in the number of samples; a target-agnostic spectral estimator attains the thresholds and the optimal weighted error, and a two-layer network whose first layer is that estimator, with a ridge readout, attains them in excess risk | Defilippis, Krzakala, Loureiro and Maillard (2026), [LIT-940](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-940.md), read in [NOTE-805](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-805.md). The optimal weighted error is Θ(α^(−1+1/(2γ))) until α ≍ m⋆^(2γ). The spectral estimator on Σ T(y_i)x_ix_iᵀ attains both (Thm. 3.6). The cascade is in the number of samples, not in training time. | [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md) v2 | Under class imbalance the last-layer geometry that unregularized cross-entropy prefers is not the simplex ETF but simplex-encoded-label interpolation: the logits equal the simplex-encoded labels, the classifier and embedding Gram matrices come from that matrix's SVD, any finite weight decay changes the geometry, and training approaches it more slowly as imbalance grows | Thrampoulidis et al. (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md). | [THEORY-289](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-289.md) v2 | For ordinary least squares on T ≥ d + 2 isotropic Gaussian covariates reused every round, with each round's labels generated by the previous fit, keeping every earlier round's data keeps the expected excess test error below π²/6 times the first fit's, though it rises every round, where replacing the data makes it grow linearly in the number of rounds | Gerstgrasser, Schaeffer, Dey et al. (2024), [LIT-971](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-971.md), read in [NOTE-815](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-815.md), Theorems 1–2 extending Dohmatob et al.'s replace result. | [THEORY-293](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-293.md) v3 | For an optimal capacity-bounded learner on an orthogonal mixture of equally frequent random facts and a second domain, the facts are learned not at all below a capacity threshold set by the mixing ratio and in full once capacity exceeds it by the facts' total entropy, and Pythia models trained on synthetic biographies mixed into web text show a threshold in model size and in mixing ratio | Gu, Lyu, Li and Zhang (2025), [LIT-984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-984.md), read in [NOTE-796](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-796.md). The theory is static. It does not say when in training the facts arrive, and it does not show that SGD reaches the optimal allocation. | Active |
| [THEORY-294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-294.md) v3 | For a wide two-layer ReLU network with zero bias on one-dimensional data whose two classes lie on opposite sides of the origin, the tangent kernel is a constant multiple of the initialization kernel, so lazy training leaves the within-class variability of its features, NC1, where initialization put it | Kothapalli & Tirer (2024), [LIT-985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-985.md), read in [NOTE-774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-774.md). NC1 = tr Σ_W / tr Σ_B of kernel-defined features is a ratio of linear functionals of the kernel matrix (Theorem 4.1). For one-dimensional data, two classes on opposite sides of the origin and zero bias, the ReLU tangent kernel of a wide two-layer net is a constant multiple of the NNGP kernel, so NC1 is the same (Theorem 5.1, re-derived). In higher dimensions it is measured no lower, and for ReLU higher; whether lazy training leaves NC1 in place there is [QUESTION-192](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-192.md). The inference that collapse requires feature learning is the reading's, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-314](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-314.md) v2 | Every minimizer of an arbitrary cost on the training outputs plus a strictly increasing function of the RKHS norm lies in the span of the kernel functions at the training points, by the reproducing property and orthogonal decomposition alone | Schölkopf, Herbrich & Smola (2001), [LIT-261](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-261.md), Theorem 1 with its proof (eqs. 18–24), read in [NOTE-836](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-836.md) and checked. The theorem is stated over countable kernel expansions of finite norm, assumes a minimizer exists, and does not cover costs that see f other than through its values at the training points. | Active |
| [THEORY-318](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-318.md) v2 | A bound k on the max-information between a dataset and an analyst's chosen statistic multiplies by at most 2^k the probability that the statistic overfits that dataset, and an ε-differentially private mechanism on datasets of n points keeps k at most log₂e·εn, whatever the distribution on datasets | Dwork, Feldman, Hardt, Pitassi, Reingold & Roth (2015), [LIT-964](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-964.md), Supplementary Material only, read in [NOTE-848](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-848.md) (Skimmed: the main text was not reached). Theorem 2 and Lemma 5 are proved there and were checked: P[overfit] ≤ 2^{I∞}·max P[overfit], and ε-DP gives I∞ ≤ log₂e·εn. Thresholdout's guarantee (Theorem 11), n = O(ln(m/β)/τ²·min{B, √(B ln(m/β))/τ}), is stated with its proof elsewhere. Statistical queries on a discrete universe only, and a procedure that prevents inflation, not a correction for a search already run. | Active |
| [THEORY-319](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-319.md) v2 | When two views are redundant for a label, the predictor that infers one view from the other is within εX + 2√(εXεZ) + εZ of the Bayes predictor in mean squared error, and it is linear in the contrastive density ratio, so for a bounded label and a square-integrable ratio a linear readout of m random evaluations of the exact ratio approaches it at rate 1/m, with no symmetry between the views required | Tosh, Krishnamurthy & Hsu (2021), [LIT-251](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-251.md), read in [NOTE-841](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-841.md): Lemma 1, §2.3–2.4, Lemma 2 and Theorem 3. | [THEORY-320](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-320.md) v2 | In a spectral contrastive graph that joins labelled known classes to unlabelled data, a novel labelling's linear-probe residual is exactly its part outside the top eigenspace that the labelled rows of the discarded eigenvectors cannot absorb, so which partition of the unlabelled data is discovered depends on the known classes: ones sharing the target's attribute can remove the residual, and ones sharing a rival attribute can raise it | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). On the population graph, at the exact rank-k optimum, R(U*, y) = ‖(I − P_{L♭})U♭ᵀy‖² (Theorem 5.5, stated as ≤, proved as = in C.1). In a one-sample-per-kind toy, a known class sharing colour makes a colour labelling recoverable, and one sharing shape makes it worse than none (Lemma 5.4). The general error bound (Theorem 5.6) is approximate and pools all known classes into one block, and is not part of this account. Nothing here is about trained networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-331](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-331.md) | Counting the inference a model will serve as well as its training, the least-compute way to reach a fixed quality shifts toward up-front compute as expected inference volume grows: a smaller model trained on more data in Sardana et al., a larger pretrained model over test-time search in Snell et al.; test-time compute won only at low volume and on questions the small model already sometimes solved | Sardana et al. (2024; arXiv 2023), [LIT-1070](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1070.md), read in [NOTE-881](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-881.md), and Snell et al. (2024), [LIT-1063](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1063.md), read in [NOTE-869](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-869.md). Sardana et al. minimise training plus lifetime inference FLOPs at a fixed loss under a Chinchilla-fitted law: the optimum moves to smaller models trained longer as known demand grows (28% fewer FLOPs at 30B quality and 10^13 inference tokens), and 47 runs show loss still falling at extreme ratios but more slowly than the law predicts. Snell et al. match FLOPs between a small model with test-time search or revision and a ~14× larger model on MATH: test-time compute wins at a low ratio of inference to pretraining tokens on easier questions and loses at a high ratio, and on the hardest at every ratio. Both take expected use as a known aggregate; neither has staleness or uncertainty about demand, and Snell's evidence is one model family on 500 questions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-342](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-342.md) | In AlphaZero on 9×9 Hex, at fixed playing strength, training compute and tree-search compute substitute along a straight line in log–log space, about 15× less search for each 10× more training over about two decades of training compute, down to a one-node search; the trade is measured for one search and counts no games played | Jones (2021), [LIT-1069](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1069.md), read in [NOTE-884](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-884.md). Across about 200 AlphaZero models on Hex boards 3×3 to 9×9, the best Elo for a given training compute follows one change-point curve, shifted by a fixed factor of compute per board row. On 9×9 only, iso-Elo contours of training against test-time search compute are straight in log–log space (fit: log test = −1.2·log train + 0.004·Elo + 29) over roughly 1e14–1e16 FLOPS-seconds of training, ending at a one-node search. One game, one nonstandard implementation, no uncertainty on the fitted coefficients, and no count of how many searches the trained agent will run, so it gives an exchange rate, not an amortization. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-349](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-349.md) | For binary outcomes and a fixed representation of individuals, a predictor can pass every test in a bounded class without being close to nature: outcome indistinguishability to tests that see the sampled prediction is equivalent, with stated losses, to multicalibration over a closely related class of sets, a predictor meeting it exists at size polynomial in the tests' size and the tolerance whatever nature's complexity, and learning one is as hard as weak agnostic learning of the class | Dwork, Kim, Reingold, Rothblum and Yona (2021), [LIT-1068](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1068.md), read in [NOTE-885](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-885.md), and Hébert-Johnson, Kim, Reingold and Rothblum (2018), [LIT-1052](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1052.md), read in [NOTE-879](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-879.md). A predictor is outcome indistinguishable relative to a class of distinguishers when none can tell nature's outcomes from outcomes drawn from the predictor, up to ε. With no access or sample access to the predictor this is equivalent to multi-accuracy or multicalibration over closely related classes, and a predictor meeting it exists at size O(s/ε²) (O(s/α⁴γ) for multicalibration), independent of nature. Learning a multicalibrated predictor is equivalent to weak agnostic learning of the class. Adequacy here is relative to the class, the outcome and the features, and is not unique; it is not closeness to the truth, and the papers say nothing about signal detection. | Active |
| [THEORY-354](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-354.md) | An observer's power to refute a predictor depends on its access to the predictor as well as on its budget: against tests that see only the sampled prediction a predictor of size O(s/ε²) always passes, but if fine-grained clique counting is hard, or BPP ≠ PSPACE, some cheap tests that may query the predictor adaptively pass only predictors about as costly as nature's own | Dwork, Kim, Reingold, Rothblum and Yona (2021), [LIT-1068](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1068.md), read in [NOTE-885](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-885.md). Against sample-access distinguishers of size s an outcome-indistinguishable predictor of size O(s/ε²) always exists. Against oracle-access distinguishers, under fine-grained hardness of clique counting or BPP ≠ PSPACE, there are natures and polynomially many cheap distinguishers such that no predictor much cheaper than nature is indistinguishable. Non-adaptive queries add little; the power comes from adaptive queries. The results are conditional and asymptotic, with upper and lower bounds in different parameterisations; they say nothing about human observers or about which access a real auditor has. | Active |
| [THEORY-359](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-359.md) | Cognitive mechanisms can be derived as the one, among those a brain can execute, that best trades the expected utility of its result against the opportunity cost of the time and resources it uses; the review shows the derivation reproducing many heuristics and biases, not that people are optimal, and the objective is per episode | Lieder & Griffiths (2020; online 2019), [LIT-1071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1071.md), read in [NOTE-873](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-873.md). Resource rationality picks the heuristic that maximizes expected utility of its result minus the expected opportunity cost of the time and resources it uses (Eq. 3), averaged over environments consistent with what is known (Eq. 4), and a five-step method derives process models from it. The support is a review of others' models recast in this frame, with numbers from those studies. The authors offer optimality as a methodological device, not a claim about people, and the method lets constraints be refitted to data. The objective is per episode, with no terms for storing, retrieving or reusing a result, or for its going stale. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-439](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-439.md) | Given the same few demonstrations, temporarily updating a language model's weights on them and then conditioning beats conditioning alone, most on tasks with structural rules or distribution shift and most when the update is trained in the in-context format: for models of 1–8B parameters, examples used as context and the same examples used as a training signal are not interchangeable | Akyürek et al. (2024; ICML 2025), [LIT-796](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-796.md), read in [NOTE-637](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-637.md). On BIG-Bench Hard with Llama 3.1 8B and 10 demonstrations over five seeds, zero-shot 40.9%, in-context 50.5%, per-task LoRA test-time training then in-context 57.8%; 12 of 27 tasks gain at least 2 points, and Boolean expressions falls. Training the update on leave-one-out in-context tasks beats training on bare pairs (57.8% against 51.5%). The update is discarded after each task, so it is as transient as a context. It is two benchmarks and one model family, and which task property predicts the gain is open. | Active |
| [THEORY-481](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-481.md) v2 | A linear-attention layer trained on in-context regression learns as a two-layer linear network does: when tasks share the input covariance's eigenbasis and the weights stay aligned with it, then in the long-context limit each input mode is learned on its own logistic curve whose timescale falls with the square of its variance, so learning is staged by the input spectrum, and the layer converges to a preconditioned estimator; at finite context length the modes decouple exactly only when inputs are isotropic, and otherwise couple at order 1/N | Mainali & Teixeira (2025), [LIT-859](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-859.md), read in [NOTE-658](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-658.md). The prediction of one linear-attention layer reduces to p₂ W Σ̂_x q₁ x_q, a product of two learned factors, so averaged gradient flow decouples into modes with τ_α dp_α/dt = q_α(1 − p_α q_α s^∞_α) and τ_α = (ηP s_α²)⁻¹, logistic from a balanced start. The fixed point ŷ = W Σ̂_x [((N+1)/N)Σ_x + (Tr Σ_x/N)I]⁻¹ x_q is the one Ahn et al. and Zhang, Frei & Bartlett found; the trajectory is new. The decoupling into independent modes is exact as N → ∞. At finite N it holds only for isotropic inputs with equal modes: the paper commutes the non-diagonal empirical covariance at (A71) and (A73), and the correct Wishart moment couples the modes at order 1/N. Alignment of the weights with the data's eigenbasis is assumed throughout, the null blocks vanish only in expectation over tasks, and the transfer to non-linear transformers is timing coincidences. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-510](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-510.md) | How much of an ImageNet image a crop must keep for its label to survive varies widely by class, with architectures agreeing on which classes are fragile, and strengthening random crop raises mean accuracy while some classes lose 20 points or more; how many classes lose is not established | Balestriero, Bottou & LeCun (2022), [LIT-234](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-234.md), read in [NOTE-845](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-845.md). Six pretrained models on cropped test images keep some classes recognisable at an 8% crop and lose others below about 50%, and agree on which. Over 20 ResNet-50 runs, moving the crop lower bound from 100% to 8% raises mean accuracy from about 70% to 76% while "academic gown" falls from about 62% to 40%. The classes shown are hand-picked; the per-class test rejects for 4.4% of classes at the 5% level, uncorrected for 1,000 tests, which alone is not more than chance; and evaluation-set noise is not counted. Theorem 1 does not reach which classes pay. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-521](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-521.md) | In the thermodynamic limit, with examples and capacity growing together at fixed load, generalization error can jump discontinuously with the load when the entropy of hypotheses just above the best error vanishes faster than the training-error energy grows: a spherical perceptron's error falls smoothly as 1/α, an Ising perceptron's drops to zero at a critical load | Martin & Mahoney (2017), [LIT-672](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-672.md), read in [NOTE-542](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-542.md), restating Seung, Sompolinsky & Tishby (1992) and Haussler, Kearns, Seung & Tishby (1996), which the record does not hold. Generalization is set by maximizing s(ε) − α ln(1/(1 − ε)). For weights on a sphere s(ε) ~ ln ε and ε ~ 1/α; for ±1 weights s(ε) ~ −(π²/2)ε² ln ε, the first-order condition has no solution past a critical load, and the error drops to zero. Uniform bounds that see a class only through its size or VC dimension are smooth and blind to this. That deep networks have such a phase diagram is the authors' conjecture, and their mapping of label noise to load and early stopping to temperature is an analogy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-574](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-574.md) | The structural width of Xin Li's learning programme is a covering number of the margin-safe region by local pieces: its lower bounds come from metric confinement through a wedge point, not from topology, labels enter only through the margin, and the error floor below width binds only learners assembled from local experts, so it does not entail routing, nor training routing apart from the task loss | Li (2026), [LIT-376](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md) (Local Urysohn Width, v1), [LIT-375](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md) (Structural Learning Theory) and [LIT-374](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md) (Structural Decoupling), read jointly in [NOTE-323](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-323.md), [NOTE-324](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-324.md) and [NOTE-322](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-322.md). In repaired form the formal core holds: width is incomparable with the per-cell VC dimension, fewer cells than width give an error floor (under an assumption that states it), and discovering all basins costs Ω(w log w) samples. But local correctness is automatic on any connected patch, the bouquet lower bound is metric (the paper's Remark 8.11 concedes it), a global classifier has width 1 (Remark 3.4), and the additive Rademacher bound said to call for decoupled training holds for joint training too. | Active |
| [THEORY-614](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-614.md) v2 | If pretraining text is a mixture of hidden Markov models indexed by a latent concept and a model fits that distribution exactly, then a prompt of concatenated examples moves the posterior onto the prompt's concept, and the in-context predictor becomes Bayes-optimal as examples accumulate, whenever each example's evidence for the concept outweighs the cost of the improbable transitions between examples; whether trained networks learn in context this way is not shown | Xie, Raghunathan, Liang & Ma (2021), [LIT-797](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-797.md), read in [NOTE-633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-633.md). Theorem 1 is proved under Assumptions 1–5 and a distinguishability condition; Theorems 2–3 give roughly 1/k excess risk without it. The proofs were not followed in the reading. [NOTE-633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-633.md) declined a THEORY because the result is conditional on exact fit to a specific generative model, so it is a consequence of that model, not a fact about language models. It is filed Proposed under the owner's ruling, with the condition in the title. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md) | Weight decay on factors is a nuclear-norm penalty on their product: with tied weights λ‖W‖²_F = λ‖WWᵀ‖_*, and for untied factors the least (‖U‖²_F + ‖V‖²_F)/2 over UVᵀ = M is ‖M‖_*, so for any loss that sees the weights only through the product, square-penalized training is nuclear-norm-penalized training of a product of bounded rank | Boncoraglio et al. (2025), [LIT-857](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-857.md), Appendix A, read in [NOTE-661](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-661.md), and re-derived here. ‖W‖²_F = Tr(WWᵀ) = ‖WWᵀ‖_*, since a PSD matrix's singular values are its eigenvalues. For untied factors, Hölder's inequality for Schatten norms and AM–GM bound ‖M‖_* by (‖U‖²_F + ‖V‖²_F)/2 over every factorization UVᵀ = M, and the balanced SVD factorization attains it. The product's rank is bounded by the factors' inner dimension. It says nothing about what the trained product looks like, which is [THEORY-180](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-180.md)'s spectral law. | Active |
| [THEORY-735](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-735.md) | Under a local quadratic model of the loss with the greedy optimal step, per-step progress at batch size B is ΔL_max/(1 + B_noise/B), and at fixed B the steps and examples needed satisfy (S/S_min − 1)(E/E_min − 1) = 1, with E_min/S_min the progress-weighted mean of B_noise | McCandlish, Kaplan, Amodei et al. (2018), [LIT-348](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-348.md), §2 and App. D.1, as read and re-derived in [NOTE-293](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-293.md). A derivation under stated assumptions: a second-order model of the loss along the step, an unbiased minibatch gradient of covariance Σ/B, and the step size that maximises the expected decrease. It says nothing about whether real training meets those assumptions, or how well the noise scale predicts the measured critical batch, which is [THEORY-033](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-033.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-737](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-737.md) | In a spectral contrastive graph that joins labelled known classes to unlabelled data, the least-squares residual of a novel labelling on the top-k eigenspace, with the labelled entries left free, equals exactly the part of the labelling outside that eigenspace that the labelled rows of the discarded eigenvectors cannot absorb | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), Theorem 5.5 with its proof in C.1, read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). | [THEORY-738](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-738.md) | In the unconstrained-features max-margin problem with k classes under step imbalance and feature dimension at least k − 1, the unique optimal logits are the simplex-encoded labels, every margin equals one, and the classifier and embedding Gram matrices are the two square-root factors of that matrix's singular value decomposition; the geometry is the simplex equiangular tight frame exactly when the classes are balanced or there are two of them | Thrampoulidis, Kini, Vakilian and Behnia (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), Theorem 1 and Corollary 1.3, read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md) and re-derived here. By [THEORY-726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md) the problem is nuclear-norm minimisation of the logits under margin constraints. The polar factor of the simplex-encoded label matrix certifies it optimal, because under step imbalance its off-diagonal entries are negative. It does not say that gradient descent or trained networks reach this geometry, which is [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-739](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-739.md) | For the quartic proxy of word2vec with tied weights, symmetric reweighting and constant weights, the rank-d minimisers are the top d eigenvectors of the relative deviation-from-independence matrix M*, scaled by the square roots of their eigenvalues, up to rotation; and from an initialisation aligned with those eigenvectors, gradient flow acquires each one in an independent logistic rise, in order of eigenvalue | Karkada, Simon, Bahri and DeWeese (2025), [LIT-855](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md), Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, read in [NOTE-660](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-660.md) and re-derived here.
