| [THEORY-740](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-740.md) | A two-layer linear network trained by gradient flow on white inputs from a decoupled, balanced start learns each singular mode of its input–output correlation in a logistic rise that waits a time of order its inverse strength times the log of the inverse initial scale, so the modes arrive one at a time in order of strength; a single-layer network on the same data learns every mode on one timescale with no plateau, so under these conditions the stages come from the product of layers and the data's spectrum | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2014, 2019), [LIT-864](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-864.md) and [LIT-862](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md), read in [NOTE-667](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-667.md) and [NOTE-666](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-666.md), re-derived here. From a decoupled, balanced start the two-layer equations keep the SVD basis of Σyx, and each mode's strength obeys τȧ = 2a(s − a), a logistic rise. One weight matrix on the same data relaxes every mode exponentially on the one timescale τ. It does not say that random starts follow the solution, which is [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-759](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-759.md) | A six-layer, 256-unit ReLU network trained by full-batch Adam to regress a sum of sinusoids at 5 to 50 cycles on [0, 1] fits the components in order of frequency, and keeps that order when the amplitudes rise tenfold with frequency, so in this setting the order of acquisition is set by the learner and not by the strength of the target's components | Rahaman et al. (2019), [LIT-1261](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1261.md), Experiment 1, read in full in [NOTE-983](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-983.md). With equal amplitudes, and with amplitudes rising from 0.1 at 5 cycles to 1 at 50, the normalised fit \|f̃(k_i)\|/A_i reaches 1 at low frequency first. This is the reverse of the order by strength that [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md) gives for a deep linear network. One architecture, one optimiser, a 1-D input, ten runs averaged. The paper's theory gives a bound on speed, not this order. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-761](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-761.md) | A continuous piecewise-linear function on R^d with compact support has a Fourier transform that, along any fixed direction û, is bounded by C(û)k^(−2), and by C(û)k^(−d−1) whenever û is orthogonal to no edge of its linear regions, which is almost every direction; C(û) is not uniform and grows without bound near the exceptional directions; for a ReLU network without compact support the statement is not established | Rahaman et al. (2019), [LIT-1261](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1261.md), read in full in [NOTE-983](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-983.md). One integration by parts turns f̃ into a sum of polytope transforms weighted by the region gradients and divided by k. Each further step of Diaz et al.'s recursion gains another 1/k until the path reaches a face whose directions are all orthogonal to k. Generic directions reach the vertices, giving k^(−d−1), and every direction gets at least k^(−2). It is a bound on what a piecewise-linear function contains, not a statement about training. Unbounded ReLU networks fall outside it. | Active |
| [THEORY-778](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-778.md) | In the Random Hierarchy Model with v symbols per level, m rules per symbol and s-tuples, the covariance between two tokens whose lowest common ancestor is ℓ levels up has zero mean over grammars and root-mean-square size about ((1 − m/v^(s−1))/(v³ m^(2ℓ−1)))^(1/2), falling by a factor m per level, while its estimate from P sequences carries noise of about (v²P)^(−1/2), so the two meet at P_ℓ ≈ v m^(2ℓ−1)/(1 − m/v^(s−1)); all to leading order in large v and m | Cagnetta and Wyart (2024), [LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md), App. D–F, read in [NOTE-687](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-687.md); re-derived to leading order by the promotion audit and checked against exact covariances of sampled grammars. A statement about the statistics of the generative model only: it says nothing about what a trained network learns, or when, and nothing about natural language. | Active |
| [THEORY-779](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-779.md) | In Kunin et al.'s underdamped Langevin model of SGD with momentum on linear regression, with gradient-noise covariance σ²H independent of the parameters, the stationary state is Gaussian with parameter covariance ησ²H(H + λI)⁻¹/(2S(1 − β)) and velocity covariance σ²H/(S(1 − β²)): for small weight decay it spreads equally along every nonzero Hessian direction and not along the null space, each Hessian eigenmode is a damped oscillator with damping ratio (1 − β)/√(2η(1 + β)(ρ + λ)), and the expected squared step is η²σ² tr(H)/(S(1 − β²)) | Kunin et al. (2021), [LIT-1011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1011.md), §§4–6 and App. G, read in [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md); the stationary moments re-derived by the promotion audit. An exact result for a model: Σ ∝ H constant and a quadratic loss are assumptions, and nothing here says a deep network meets them. The probability current is nonzero but reversible: under the model's assumptions the stationary process is time-reversible once velocities are flipped, so it is "broken detailed balance" only in the paper's sense, a nonzero current. | Active |
| [THEORY-781](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-781.md) | Strong gradient noise in SGD, like weight decay above a threshold, makes the subspace fixed by a mirror symmetry of a network's loss attracting even where it is a saddle, so that networks trained with SGD at large learning rates or small batches reach sparse, low-rank and identical-neuron solutions, as Ziyin proposes | Ziyin (2024), [LIT-1014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1014.md), read in [NOTE-716](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-716.md). Beyond the exact half that [THEORY-213](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-213.md) holds, the paper argues by a Lyapunov-exponent analysis that strong SGD noise makes a mirror's subspace attracting even at a strict saddle, and reads sparsity, low rank and identical neurons in trained networks as its result. That analysis rests on a second-order, diagonal- Hessian approximation, and the network evidence is a ResNet18's correlation blocks. The test is [QUESTION-206](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-206.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-782](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-782.md) | In networks that learn addition from summed embeddings, the critical training fraction of grokking is the fraction at which the training set's same-answer pairs come to fix the generalising representation up to translation and scale, at every group size, as Liu, Kitouni, Nolte, Michaud, Tegmark and Williams propose | Liu, Kitouni, Nolte, Michaud, Tegmark and Williams (2022), [LIT-858](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-858.md), read in [NOTE-662](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-662.md), with Power et al.'s critical fraction ([LIT-341](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-341.md)). The paper presents the critical training fraction as where the training set's equations fix the embedding. [THEORY-181](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-181.md) holds the theorem for the ideal model and the match at the one size measured, p = 10 with 1D embeddings. Held to addition: for S₃ the networks generalise beyond this mechanism. The multi-size test is [QUESTION-199](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-199.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-783](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-783.md) v2 | In neural-network training, sign-descent-like optimizers such as Adam make independent skills of unequal frequency compete for coordinate signs, so that they are learned one after another where gradient descent would learn them together; this is one source of sequential skill onset, beside dependence between skills, as Liu, Liu, Michaud, Gore and Tegmark propose | Liu, Liu, Michaud, Gore and Tegmark (2025), [LIT-951](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-951.md), read in [NOTE-794](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-794.md). The paper explains the Domino effect, skills starting as others finish, by a coordinate-wise optimizer's competition for update signs. [THEORY-253](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-253.md) holds the simulation in their Geometry model and the rotated quadratic. The paper also shows dependent skills starting after their prerequisites (C5), so the optimizer is one source of sequential onset, not the only one. The test in a trained network is [QUESTION-193](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-193.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-784](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-784.md) | Language models trained on limited data show a test loss falling as P^(−γ/(2β)) because P training tokens resolve token correlations only out to a horizon growing as P^(1/(2β)), so that more data mainly lengthens the context a model can use, when the model learns within that horizon faster than it grows, as Cagnetta, Raventós, Ganguli and Wyart propose | Cagnetta, Raventós, Ganguli and Wyart (2026), [LIT-888](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-888.md), read in [NOTE-689](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-689.md), building on Cagnetta and Wyart's effective context window ([LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md)). The paper presents the horizon as the reason the data-limited exponent is γ/(2β). [THEORY-204](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-204.md) holds what it showed: the derivation under assumed scaling forms, and the measured overlap on TinyStories and WikiText-103 up to about 10^8 tokens. Whether the horizon is why is the test [QUESTION-233](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-233.md) asks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-786](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-786.md) | Deep networks learn hierarchically generated data from a number of examples set by when the correlations between input patches and the class rise above sampling noise, so detecting those correlations is how they learn the grammar, as Cagnetta and coauthors propose | Cagnetta, Petrini, Tomasini, Favero and Wyart (2023), [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md), propose that deep networks learn compositional data by detecting the correlations between input patches and the class, and that the sample complexity is where those correlations emerge from sampling noise. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md), the measured law and the synonym-invariance it coincides with. This is the mechanism, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-788](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-788.md) | Training a deep classifier past zero training error generally collapses its last-layer features onto their class means, drives the centred means toward a simplex equiangular tight frame aligned with the classifier, and makes the decision nearest class mean, as Papyan, Han and Donoho propose from their runs | Papyan, Han and Donoho (2020), [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md), title their paper on the "prevalence" of neural collapse and present it as a pervasive outcome of the terminal phase of training. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md), only what their runs measured: three architectures with cross-entropy on seven balanced datasets without augmentation. This is the general law, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-790](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-790.md) | In deep networks trained by SGD on real data, minibatch noise drives parameter groups related by a rescaling symmetry toward the point where their gradient noise balances, at a rate set by learning rate over batch size, so that at stationarity they sit neither where gradient flow would leave them nor spread out as under isotropic noise, as Ziyin, Li and Ueda propose | Ziyin, Li & Ueda, [LIT-1012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1012.md), read in [NOTE-714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-714.md), with the Itô term from [LIT-1013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1013.md). The law of balance is proved in the SDE model of SGD, and that part is the Active [THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md). The authors present the law as general to networks with rescaling symmetry, but test it only on small synthetic networks. This THEORY holds the general claim, for deep networks on real data, which no measurement in the record yet supports. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-792](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-792.md) | In a deep linear network trained by gradient descent from generic initial weights, not only from decoupled ones, depth slows learning through the initial end-to-end strength of each mode, so that random orthogonal weights, whose product is an isometry, learn in a number of iterations that stays bounded as depth grows, as Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli argue from simulation | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2014), [LIT-864](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-864.md), read in [NOTE-667](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-667.md). The exact depth law is proved only from decoupled, balanced starts, and that part is the Active [THEORY-187](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-187.md). Beyond it, the paper argues from MNIST runs and random-matrix simulations that random orthogonal layers are such a start in effect, because their product is an isometry, while scaled Gaussian layers are not. This THEORY holds that wider claim, which is argued and simulated and not derived. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-793](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-793.md) | Gradient flow on a symmetrized Barlow Twins loss with a linear or fixed-kernel model, from generic small initialization and not only from initialization aligned with the eigenvectors, learns the top eigenvectors of the pairs' symmetrized cross-correlation one at a time in order of eigenvalue and ends at a top spectral solution, as Simon and coauthors derive informally | Simon et al. (2023), [LIT-242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-242.md), read in [NOTE-741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-741.md). The stepwise dynamics, the minimum-norm end point and the kernel-PCA form are proved from aligned initialization, and that part is the Active [THEORY-229](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-229.md). Generic small initialization rests on the paper's Result 4.6, which its authors style a result and derive informally in App. C, with numerical checks at d = 3. This THEORY holds that generic case. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-794](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-794.md) | In vision models, compositional generalization to unseen combinations of concepts is driven by the diversity of the combinations seen in training rather than by data volume, and arrives with representations that are linearly factored by concept, as Uselis, Dittadi and Oh propose | Uselis, Dittadi & Oh (2025), [LIT-667](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-667.md), read in [NOTE-525](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-525.md). Their title and abstract present diversity of combinations, not data volume, as what drives compositional generalization in vision models. Their evidence is ResNet-50s trained from scratch on two-concept grids, with checkpoints chosen on the unseen pairs, and that measured part, with the factorization theorem, is the Active [THEORY-117](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-117.md). This THEORY holds the general causal claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-797](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-797.md) | Deep classifiers trained with MSE loss stay near the least-squares classifier for their own features and move along the central path by the dynamics of continually renormalized gradient flow, whose equal-rate growth of the whitened class-separation singular values is how they reach neural collapse, as Han, Papyan and Donoho propose | Han, Papyan & Donoho (2021; ICLR 2022), [LIT-974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-974.md), read in [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md). The paper's proposed explanation of neural collapse under MSE in real networks, filed apart from its measured central-path proximity and its derivation in a renormalized model ([THEORY-278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-278.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. Renormalization is imposed, not measured, and every experiment used weight decay, which the derivation excludes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-806](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-806.md) | Translation without parallel data, as of an unknown animal communication system into a human language, is learnable from a plausibility prior over the target language alone, with error falling as the common ground between the languages grows and as the source language grows richer | The general reading that [THEORY-270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-270.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the common-nonsense model its bound is proved in (batch 044). Goldwasser, Gruber, Kalai and Paradise (NeurIPS 2023), [LIT-941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-941.md), read in [NOTE-804](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-804.md), motivate their framework by translating animal communication and state its lesson for translation in general, while saying their stylised models are not intended to capture natural language. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-809](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-809.md) | Language models trained by gradient descent on a mixture of random facts and other data reach the capacity-optimal allocation, so the model size and the mixing ratio at which they begin to learn the facts are those of an optimal capacity-bounded learner | The link that [THEORY-293](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-293.md)'s title asserted before the promotion audit narrowed it (batch 036) to the optimal learner's theorem and the observation of a threshold in Pythia models. Gu, Lyu, Li and Zhang (2025), [LIT-984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-984.md), read in [NOTE-796](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-796.md), explain the trained models' thresholds by the optimal learner's. The one quantitative check, a size exponent of 1.152 against a predicted 1.283, is recorded against it. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-813](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-813.md) | Training a wide network in the lazy, kernel regime does not make its features more collapsed than at initialization, so neural collapse, where it occurs, is something only feature learning produces | The general reading that [THEORY-294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-294.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the one-dimensional, zero-bias, two-class case it proves. Kothapalli and Tirer (2024), [LIT-985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-985.md), read in [NOTE-774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-774.md), draw it as their conclusion: the lazy regime does not collapse anything, so the data-dependence of collapse has to come from a kernel that moves with the data. Beyond the solved case their support is simulation on two-class Gaussian data, where the NTK comes out less collapsed than the NNGP. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-839](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-839.md) | A model optimal for the distribution its own deployment induces, a performatively stable point, need not minimize the risk it actually incurs, and the gap is bounded: for a loss that is L_z-Lipschitz in the data and γ-strongly convex in the parameters, and a distribution map that is ε-Lipschitz in Wasserstein-1 distance, every stable point lies within 2L_zε/γ of every performative optimum; in a biased-coin example the stable point is µ/(1 − ε) and the optimum µ/(1 − 2ε), equal only when the prediction has no effect | Perdomo, Zrnic, Mendler-Dünner and Hardt (2020), [LIT-1336](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1336.md), read in [NOTE-1044](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1044.md). Self-consistency under one's own influence and the best outcome under that influence are different targets. The bound says they are close when the influence is weak relative to the loss's curvature. It does not say how to find the optimum, which needs the distribution map away from the deployed model. | Active |
| [THEORY-840](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-840.md) | When every log-likelihood a predictive family V can assign lies in [−B, B], the V-information estimated from N samples is within 4R_N(G_V) + 2B√(2 log(1/δ)/N) of the true V-information with probability at least 1 − 2δ, with R_N(G_V) the Rademacher complexity of the family's log-likelihoods; so usable information relative to a family of small complexity can be estimated in high dimension, and what is estimated is that family's information, not Shannon's | Xu, Zhao, Song, Stewart and Ermon (2020), [LIT-1309](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1309.md), read in [NOTE-1048](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1048.md), Theorem 1. Restricting the predictor class trades the data-processing inequality for estimability. The bound needs bounded log-likelihoods and says nothing about Shannon information, which a restricted family may under- or over-state ([THEORY-846](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-846.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-846](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-846.md) | Information usable by a predictor restricted to a family V can be created by computing on the data, so the data-processing inequality fails for V-information: with Z the exclusive-or of two fair independent bits, linear and one-coordinate families extract nothing about Z from the pair and all of it from their exclusive-or; V-information computed from any function of the source is bounded by the source's Shannon information when the family's input-free predictions can match the marginal of the target, and can exceed it otherwise | Xu, Zhao, Song, Stewart and Ermon (2020), [LIT-1309](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1309.md), read in [NOTE-1048](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1048.md), define V-information and say it "can be created through computation". The record's worked case is [CLAIM-199](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-199.md)'s XOR under the paper's linear families, and its addition is the ceiling: usable information never exceeds the source's Shannon information when V can predict the marginal of Y without input, and can exceed it when V cannot. It says nothing about which family a real observer has. | Active |
| [THEORY-861](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-861.md) | When a deployed model changes the distribution it is scored on, retraining on the distribution the last model induced contracts at rate εβ/γ, for a β-jointly smooth, γ-strongly convex loss and a distribution map that is ε-Lipschitz in Wasserstein-1 distance, and so converges to a unique performatively stable point when ε < γ/β; each condition is needed, since dropping strong convexity, joint smoothness or the bound on ε each admits a case where retraining never converges | Perdomo, Zrnic, Mendler-Dünner and Hardt (2020), [LIT-1336](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1336.md), read in [NOTE-1044](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1044.md). Retraining under performativity is a fixed-point iteration, and these are the conditions for it to settle. Its fixed point is self-consistent, not optimal ([THEORY-839](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-839.md)), and outside the conditions there may be several or none. | Active |
| [THEORY-899](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-899.md) | In an infinite, well-mixed population whose members each sample the quality of their own type, imitation of success has the expected update of a single Cross Learning bandit agent (the Taylor replicator dynamic), and the weighted voter model, in which members broadcast their type in proportion to their sample and adopt the first type they perceive, has the expected update of Maynard-Cross Learning, π_a ← π_a + (r_k / v^π)(1[a = k] − π_a), the Maynard-Smith replicator dynamic; the population vector is the policy and no member learns | Soma et al.'s Propositions 1 and 2, read in full from arXiv v6 in [NOTE-1132](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1132.md), with both proofs and the aggregation in Eqs. 8–14 re-derived. An exact identity of expected updates under idealizing assumptions: infinite N, large well-mixed neighbourhoods, and imitation decoupled from evaluation. Each member is one parallel action sample, α = 1/N plays the learning rate, and the macro-policy is a stateless bandit policy over the members' types. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-905](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-905.md) | In simulations of the two imitation protocols, populations small enough to be finite often settle on a suboptimal option because pure imitation can remove a type entirely, and once settled the protocols give no way to re-explore when the environment changes; variants in which members compare quality estimates converge faster than blind weighted voting, at the cost of more communication and comparison | Soma et al.'s simulations and limits section, read in [NOTE-1132](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1132.md). With ten options and arbitrary parameters that the authors call qualitative, swarms of about 500 track the replicator dynamic and smaller ones often lock onto worse options. The authors state that pure imitation can delete a type and has no mechanism for escape in non-stationary environments. Hybrids that compare qualities are faster. Simulation-scoped, not a theorem. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-925](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-925.md) | In a cooperative stochastic game with decentralised actors and a centralised critic, a baseline for each agent that averages the critic's value over that agent's own alternative actions under its own policy, the other agents' actions held fixed, leaves the expected policy gradient unchanged, so each agent can be credited with the advantage of its actual action over that counterfactual average without a default action or an extra simulation; the counterfactual values come from the learned critic, not from the environment | Foerster et al.'s counterfactual baseline (COMA, Eq. 4 and Appendix A of arXiv v3), read in full in [NOTE-1152](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1152.md), with the zero-expectation step re-derived. A proved property of the estimator, not of performance. Its counterfactual is "had the agent acted as it usually does", not "had it not acted", and its values are a learned critic's, trained on occasions when each alternative was taken; it presupposes those occasions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-927](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-927.md) | In a sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layer trained without balancing losses, the gate came to give large weights to the same few experts, which the authors attribute to self-reinforcement, favoured experts being trained more and so selected more; in one 256-expert language model, the squared coefficient of variation of expert importance or load as an auxiliary loss reduced the peak-to-mean load from 17.8 to at most 1.47 and test perplexity from 39.8 to 35.6–35.7 | Shazeer et al. (2017), section 4 and Appendix A, read in full in [NOTE-1145](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1145.md) from arXiv v1. The imbalance is reported in one paragraph, with Table 6's no-loss row as its evidence: one architecture, ten epochs, no variance. The mechanism is the authors' explanation, not a tested result. The fix penalizes unequal use regardless of competence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-928](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-928.md) | Two softmax reinforcement learners whose reward memories decay at rate α follow coupled replicator equations plus a term α Σ x_j log(x_j / x_i) toward uniform play; without decay the dynamics are conservative, Hamiltonian in zero-sum games, and with decay they are dissipative | Sato & Crutchfield (arXiv 2002; PRE 2003), [LIT-1520](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1520.md), read in full from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1144](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1144.md), Eqs. 1–13. The entropy-like term is what memory decay becomes under softmax choice; re-derived in the reading. The model updates every action's memory at the same rate, so it is the full-information case, not Q-learning as usually run. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-929](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-929.md) | A joint action-value that is a non-decreasing function of per-agent values, each conditioning only on its agent's own history, makes the profile of the agents' individually greedy actions a greedy joint action, which suffices for decentralised greedy execution and is strictly more expressive than a sum; it cannot represent a joint value in which an agent's best action depends on what the others do at the same step | Rashid et al.'s QMIX (ICML 2018), read in full in [NOTE-1154](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1154.md), with QTRAN ([NOTE-1141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1141.md)) for the strictness. Monotonicity is sufficient for the greedy-profile property and not necessary. It presupposes a real- valued joint value: what it adds is that each member's ranking of its own actions agrees with the collective's whatever the others do, an ordinal separability condition. It is Wolpert and Tumer's factoredness stated for values. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-930](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-930.md) | In empirical games built from about a thousand sampled search agents in eight small board games, and in the AlphaStar league, Nash cluster size peaks at intermediate transitive strength and narrows toward the strongest and the weakest strategies, while Blotto, the disc game, Kuhn poker and noisy Elo games do not show that profile | Czarnecki et al. (2020), [LIT-1504](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1504.md), section 6 and supplements E–I, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1146.md). Agents were MinMax at depths 0–9, loss-seeking MaxMin and MCTS, with 50 seeds each, about 1000 distinct per game after duplicates were removed. Games: Hex, Go and Quoridor on small boards, Tic-Tac-Toe, its misère form and Connect Four. AlphaStar's league shows its training system's geometry, the authors say. A qualitative profile with a fitted skew-normal curve and no test. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-931](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-931.md) | A learner that ascends its own return after one anticipated naive gradient step of its opponent, differentiating through that step, reached tit-for-tat-like reciprocity in 81% of fifty exact-gradient runs of the memory-one iterated prisoner's dilemma, where pairs of naive gradient learners ended at the mutual-defection return, and settled at the mixed equilibrium of iterated matching pennies where naive learners did not converge; shown for two players, one-step shaping and access to the opponent's parameters | Foerster et al.'s LOLA (AAMAS 2018), read in full in [NOTE-1150](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1150.md) from arXiv v4, with the update rule re-derived. Empirical, in two small games and a grid game. Shaping here is mutual and produced cooperation, not capture; in matching pennies, a harmonic game, it damped the cycling of naive learners. Table 3's naive-learner tit-for-tat figure (20.8%) does not square with their return (−1.98), and the NOTE says so. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-932](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-932.md) | The replicator-plus-entropy model of Boltzmann Q-learning in two-player stateless games is exact for frequency-adjusted Q-learning, not for Q-learning, whose expected update carries an extra factor of each action's selection probability and whose trajectories in 2×2 games depart from the model depending on initialization | Kaisers & Tuyls (AAMAS 2010), [LIT-1511](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1511.md), read in full in [NOTE-1140](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1140.md), correcting the model of Tuyls, Verbeeck & Lenaerts (2003), [LIT-1501](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1501.md), which is not read. The derivation of the discrepancy is short and was checked in the reading; the experiments are three games, one temperature, compared by eye. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-933](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-933.md) | Individual-Global-Max, that the agents' individually greedy actions form a greedy joint action, is strictly weaker than additive or monotonic factorisation: every single-state matrix game with a unique optimum satisfies it, yet in 177 of 310 random three-by-three two-agent games value-decomposition and monotonic mixing failed to learn the optimal joint action that an IGM-only method found; a sufficient condition is that the sum of individual values, shifted by a state value, equals the joint value at the greedy profile and bounds it from above elsewhere | Son et al.'s QTRAN (ICML 2019), read in full in [NOTE-1141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1141.md), with Theorem 1 and the single-state observation re-derived. IGM presupposes a real-valued joint value and constrains only the optimum: members may rank everything below it differently from the collective. With full observability it is nearly empty; its content is whether members acting on local histories can each pick their part of the optimum. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-936](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-936.md) | In two-agent rock–scissors–paper played by softmax reinforcement learners, nonzero tie rewards give quasiperiodic tori and Hamiltonian chaos without memory decay, and limit cycles and chaotic attractors with it, over a large share of the tie-reward range simulated | Sato & Crutchfield (arXiv 2002; PRE 2003), [LIT-1520](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1520.md), read in full in [NOTE-1144](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1144.md), pp. 2–3 and Figs. 1–3. Numerical results for one game, two agents and the parameters shown; the zero-decay, zero-sum case was first reported in Sato, Akiyama and Farmer (PNAS 2002), which is not held. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-937](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-937.md) | When a mixture of experts is trained on the error of a single expert chosen stochastically by the gate, or on the negative log-likelihood of the mixture, an expert that fits a case better than the gate-weighted average gains responsibility for it; on a four-class vowel task, mixtures of 4 or 8 linear experts learned in about half the epochs of backpropagation networks of equal size, at equal accuracy, and divided the task by class pair, leaving all but 2 or 3 experts with mixing proportions effectively zero | Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan and Hinton (1991), read in full in [NOTE-1147](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1147.md) from a scan of the published article. The gradients of Eqs. 1.4 and 1.5 were re-derived when filed. The task is small (two formants, 75 speakers, 25 runs per system) and has two natural subtasks; the idle experts are read by the authors as economy, and their recovery is not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-941](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-941.md) | If every player of a finite game switches from its last action to each other action with probability proportional to its positive conditional regret, the empirical distribution of play converges almost surely to the set of correlated equilibria | Hart & Mas-Colell (Econometrica 2000; handout 1996), [LIT-1521](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1521.md), read in full in [NOTE-1142](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1142.md). Convergence is of time-averaged joint frequencies to a set, not of play to an equilibrium; the common history is the correlating device; inertia is needed; and interior correlated equilibria that are not pure Nash cannot be the limit. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-945](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-945.md) | When each agent's Q-function is approximated as an average of pairwise terms and expanded about the mean action of its neighbours, the first-order term vanishes and the approximation error is a second-order remainder bounded by the curvature of the pairwise Q-function, leaving a two-body problem between an agent and its neighbours' average; with homogeneous agents, mean field Q-learning converges to the Nash Q-value under assumptions the authors call strong, and learned tasks of 500 and 1000 agents where independent and centralized-critic baselines failed | Yang et al. (2018), read in full in [NOTE-1148](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1148.md) from arXiv v5. The expansion and the remainder bound were re-derived when filed; the appendix states an equality where only an inequality holds, which leaves the bound intact. The cancellation of remainders is argued from homogeneity, not proved, and the contraction step needs a high temperature while the convergence theorem assumes a greedy limit. The approximation requires agents interchangeable within a neighbourhood. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-947](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-947.md) | For Blackwell approachability of an approachable polytope under partial monitoring with a known signal law, there are efficient algorithms whose average vector payoff reaches the target at expected distance O(T^-1/3) for general signals and O(T^-1/2) when the signal law does not depend on the decision, the worst-case optimal rates for those two classes | Kwon and Perchet (2017), [LIT-1526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1526.md), read in [NOTE-1159](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1159.md). The rates are for the average payoff's distance to the target, uniformly over Nature's choices, with approachability assumed (Perchet's condition). Optimal means not improvable in the worst case over games. It gives no guarantee for individual stages or rolling windows, and none when the signal law is unknown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-950](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-950.md) | For a finite partial-monitoring game in which every two actions whose cells meet can estimate their loss difference from their own two signals, RelExp3's expected regret satisfies lim sup E[R_n]/√n ≤ 8√(2K_loc(1+F)(2+F) log K), with K_loc the most actions whose cells share a point and F the number of feedback symbols, and no other game-dependent constant; a two-action game shows that a factor linear in F cannot be avoided in general | Lattimore and Szepesvári (2019), [LIT-1524](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1524.md), read in [NOTE-1162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1162.md). For the class of games Bartók (2013) studied, the leading constant of the √n regret depends only on K_loc, F and log K, asymptotically. It is the first such result against adversaries. The constant reached before the asymptotics set in still depends on large game constants. It is a bound for one algorithm in a sub-class of the easy games, not a characterisation of the constant. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-957](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-957.md) | When the signal law depends on the decision, Kwon and Perchet's approachability algorithm learns what each decision would reveal only from the stages on which it is played: it keeps every decision's probability at least γ/\|I\| and estimates the flag by importance weighting, an estimate that is conditionally unbiased with second moment Σ_i 1/P[i_t = i] ≤ \|I\|²/γ, with the tuned floor γ shrinking as T^-1/3; when the signal law does not depend on the decision, the raw signal is already unbiased for every component and no floor is used | Kwon and Perchet (2017), [LIT-1526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1526.md), read in [NOTE-1159](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1159.md). Under decision-dependent partial monitoring, information about a decision's signal comes only from playing it, and its unbiased estimate costs variance inversely proportional to the probability of playing it. A floor is how the algorithm keeps that finite. That the floor is necessary in general is supported by the matching lower bound, not shown here. Nothing here says what floor a non-learning system should keep. | Active |
| [THEORY-961](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-961.md) | In a finite partial-monitoring game, an action optimal wherever two neighbouring actions tie has a loss vector on the segment between theirs, so a degenerate or duplicate action never creates a neighbouring pair or decides the trivial class, yet its signals count toward the pair's local observability; and the T^2/3 lower bound for a pair that is not locally observable needs the separating direction in the kernel of the signal matrices of all such actions, not only of the two neighbours | Lattimore and Szepesvári (2019), [LIT-1524](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1524.md), read in [NOTE-1162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1162.md), on Bartók et al. (2014), [LIT-1528](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1528.md). Of actions optimal only on a boundary: "Although these actions are never uniquely optimal, they can be informative". They enter the classification only through the neighbourhood set N_ab. Bartók et al.'s lower-bound proof chose the separating direction in the kernel of the two neighbours' signals alone. With such an action informative, that direction can be told apart cheaply. The fix is to take it in the kernel of every action in N_ab, which the definition of local observability already provides. It says what such actions contribute, not how often an algorithm must play them. | Active |
| [THEORY-962](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-962.md) v2 | In a finite partial-monitoring game, the signals of a set D of actions determine the expected loss difference of actions i and j under every outcome distribution iff ℓ_i − ℓ_j lies in the sum of the row spaces of their signal matrices; when it does not, two outcome distributions differing along a vector in the common kernel give every action in D the same signal law and reverse the preference between i and j, so no amount of play restricted to D can learn the comparison | Bartók, Foster, Pál, Rakhlin and Szepesvári (2014), [LIT-1528](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1528.md), read in [NOTE-1164](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1164.md). Observability in partial monitoring is a linear-algebra condition on the loss and signal matrices: a comparison is learnable from some actions exactly when its loss difference is in the span of their signal row spaces. Global and local observability are the two choices of D the classification uses. It says what can be estimated, not how fast; the rates are [THEORY-964](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-964.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-963](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-963.md) | The minimax regret of every finite partial-monitoring game against an oblivious adversary, degenerate and duplicate actions included, is 0 when no two actions are neighbours, Θ̃(√n) when every pair of neighbours is locally observable, Θ(n^2/3) when every pair is globally but some pair is not locally observable, and linear otherwise; its lower bounds are proved against stochastic outcomes, so the same four classes hold for them | Lattimore and Szepesvári (2019), [LIT-1524](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1524.md), read in [NOTE-1162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1162.md), completing Bartók et al. (2014), [LIT-1528](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1528.md). The four classes, trivial, easy, hard and hopeless, now cover every finite game. Two things change from Bartók et al.'s statement: the adversarial half no longer excludes degenerate and duplicate actions, and the trivial class is "no pair of neighbouring actions", not "one non-dominated action", which misplaces games whose extra actions are degenerate or duplicates. It classifies the best policy in a fixed, known game, up to game-dependent constants. It does not cover a learner barred from some actions, feedback that changes during play, or adaptive adversaries. | Active |
| [THEORY-964](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-964.md) v3 | The minimax regret of a finite partial-monitoring game takes one of four rates, decided by its loss and signal matrices: 0 when only one action is non-dominated, Θ̃(√T) when every pair of neighbouring actions is locally observable, Θ(T^2/3) when the game is globally but not locally observable, and Θ(T) when it is not globally observable; against stochastic opponents for every game, against oblivious adversaries for non-degenerate games | Bartók, Foster, Pál, Rakhlin and Szepesvári (2014), [LIT-1528](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1528.md), read in [NOTE-1164](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1164.md). Four classes, trivial, easy, hard and hopeless, with conditions checkable from the matrices before play. It classifies the best policy for a fixed, known game. It does not cover a policy that is barred from some actions, a feedback structure that changes during play, or finite-horizon constants, and its adversarial half excludes degenerate games. | Superseded — by [THEORY-963](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-963.md) |
| [THEORY-967](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-967.md) | In a two-layer attention-only transformer, attention heads change function during training: heads in the first layer that predict simple n-grams early later become the previous-token heads of the induction circuit, a bracket-matching support head, or supporting members of a circuit with second-layer n-gram heads, giving up simple n-grams as they do, and particular n-grams pass from one head to another; so later circuits form partly by repurposing components that already had a role | Wang, Hoogland, van Wingerden, Furman and Murfet (2024), [LIT-1535](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1535.md), read in [NOTE-1188](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1188.md). "Heads 0:1, 0:4, 0:7 ultimately become the two previous-token heads and (layer 0) Dyck head respectively. However, these heads appear to start out as simple n-gram heads." Layer-0 multigram heads lose information about simple n-grams from stage LM3, as path patching and composition scores show them coming to feed layer-1 bracket-matching heads. The "ago" n-gram moves from head 0:0 to head 1:0. Whether the late roles are built from the early ones, or merely follow them in time, is not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-973](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-973.md) v2 | In small attention-only transformer language models of two to six layers, in-context learning, measured as the loss at token 500 minus the loss at token 50, appears abruptly in one early window of training in which induction heads form, and ablating those heads at test time removes nearly all of it; one-layer models show neither, and letting a single layer attend by the previous token brings the jump to one-layer models and moves it earlier in two-layer ones | Olsson et al. (2022), [LIT-1538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1538.md), read in [NOTE-1173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1173.md): Arguments 1–3 for the small attention-only series, with the smeared-key models. The score jumps from under 0.15 to about 0.4 nats in the window where induction heads form, pattern-preserving ablation of the induction heads removes nearly all of it to the end of training, and an architecture that lets one layer express induction moves the jump. It says nothing causal about models with MLPs or large models, and nothing about few-shot task learning, which the score does not measure. | Active |
| [THEORY-975](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-975.md) | In a two-layer attention-only transformer trained on the Pile, the weight-refined local learning coefficients of individual attention heads start alike and diverge over training, and clustering the curves groups the heads by the functional types that ablation assigns them at the end of training, previous-token, current-token, induction and n-gram-memorizing; among layer-1 heads, those running simple algorithms end with the lowest values and those memorizing the most n-grams with the highest | Wang, Hoogland, van Wingerden, Furman and Murfet (2024), [LIT-1535](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1535.md), read in [NOTE-1188](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1188.md): §4.1, Figs. 1–2 and 11, appendices B, F.5 and G. Per-head curves of how degenerate the loss is in that head's weights separate the heads by what they end up doing, and the separation is in the curves' shapes over training, not only their end values. It is one small model, cluster counts chosen by eye, and estimates whose ordering, not value, the authors trust. It does not show that the coefficient predicts a head's type before the type is visible. | Active |
| [THEORY-981](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-981.md) | When a data distribution is unchanged by a group of orthogonal transformations under which a network is equivariant, the weights fixed by that group form a subspace that population gradient descent never leaves; for attention-only transformers on block-list inductive tasks, with fixed orthogonal write maps, Musat, Pimentel, Zucchet and Hofmann compute this subspace as the span of a few elementary token and position actions composed through the heads, and an elementwise optimizer such as sign descent keeps it only when those actions are aligned with the parameter coordinates | Musat et al. (2026), [LIT-1530](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1530.md), read in [NOTE-1177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1177.md). Symmetries of the data confine population gradient descent to the weights those symmetries fix; for their task class and idealized architecture this is a subspace whose coordinates are interpretable head actions. It does not say the subspace is attractive (the paper proves only invariance), and it does not cover minibatch noise beyond expectation, learnable value maps (a sketch in the paper), or adaptive optimizers, which keep it only when the basis is coordinate-aligned. | Active |
| [THEORY-990](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-990.md) v2 | In transformer language models of every size, including large ones with MLPs, induction heads, extended to fuzzy matching of similar tokens and abstract patterns, are the mechanism of most in-context learning, as Olsson et al. propose | Olsson et al. (2022), [LIT-1538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1538.md), read in [NOTE-1173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1173.md). The paper's thesis: circuits with the induction head's mechanism, matching "[A*][B*] … [A] → [B], where A* ≈ A and B* ≈ B are similar in some space", "implement most in-context learning in large models". For large models the authors grade their own evidence correlational (Argument 1), weakly interventional (Argument 2), plausibility (Argument 4) and analogy (Argument 6). Their strongest alternative is that other composition heads, formed in the same window, carry more of it above some size. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-997](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-997.md) | When a pretrained language model is fine-tuned on a task it initially fails, it acquires the task mainly by reconnecting components it already has rather than by recruiting new ones: the circuits found before and after keep most of their nodes and change most of their edges, as Wang, Hu, Du, Cheng, Wang and Zou propose from LoRA fine-tuning of Pythia-1.4B on arithmetic | Wang et al. (2025), [LIT-1539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1539.md), read in [NOTE-1183](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1183.md). Their EAP-IG circuits (top 5% of edges) change edges 2.8–4.3 times as much as nodes over LoRA fine-tuning on five arithmetic tasks. A record simulation shows that a fixed edge budget on a transformer-sized graph gives the same contrast when only edge-level noise is resampled, so the counts do not yet show reorganization. Fine-tuning only, one model for most results, arithmetic only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1001.md) | In a transformer whose candidate circuits are sets of shared elementary coordinates, how circuits interact during training is set by what they share: circuits that share a unit cooperate, and circuits that need the same layers for different roles compete, so that which circuit wins is decided by the initialization of units beyond its own, with sharp boundaries between competitors and soft ones between cooperators, as Musat, Pimentel, Zucchet and Hofmann read their three-layer scan | Musat et al. (2026), [LIT-1530](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1530.md), read in [NOTE-1177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1177.md). In projected SGD training of a three-layer single-head attention-only transformer on in-context bigrams, three induction circuits are possible, and the winner depends on initial strengths outside the winner itself. The authors explain the pattern by cooperation through a shared unit and competition for layers. The evidence is one scan over two initial strengths with every other coordinate zeroed, in projected training. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1009](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1009.md) | In Musat, Pimentel, Zucchet and Hofmann's two-layer attention-only transformer on in-context bigrams, once an in-weights circuit that maps each common token to its memorized partner has saturated, the population gradient on the induction circuit is what it would be without it multiplied by fr + (1 − fr)fv, the share of the data the memorized map does not solve, up to errors that vanish at large vocabulary and large in-weights margin when no distractor block carries the query's partner; the two circuits occupy orthogonal coordinates and still interact, because they solve overlapping parts of the data | Musat et al. (2026), [LIT-1530](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1530.md), read in [NOTE-1177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1177.md). A memorized shortcut that solves part of the data removes the in-context circuit's gradient on that part and leaves the rest. It is a theorem in an idealized model under a disjointness assumption (A4) that the paper's own sampler violates, at a cost it states. It does not say the observed order in the paper's one run is due to it: there fr = 0.9 and the factor is 0.9. | Active |
| [THEORY-1057](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1057.md) | Gradient descent with backpropagation, weight decay and Newton's method are one discrete-time semantics of an operad of potential-carrying lenses, in which the state moves by subtracting the sharpened sum of three pulled-back covectors (from the output, from the input wiring and from the potential); the semantics is an operad functor, so a composite's update is assembled from its parts' updates, and backpropagation is that functoriality | Spivak (2026), [LIT-1649](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1649.md), read in [NOTE-1225](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1225.md) from arXiv v2. Lens internalization (Corollary 3.3.4) and an integrator give operad functors ArrSm → PC (Theorem 4.3.6, Corollary 6.4.1). Under the configuration integrator the state update is q ↦ q − ♯_q(ξ_Q), with ξ_Q the Q*-component of the sum in (58); a parameterized map wired to a loss gives gradient descent (76), a weight-only potential gives weight decay (Proposition 7.2.3), and an inverse-Hessian response gives Newton's method (67). Active as mathematics. Per datum, deterministic, explicit-Euler; Adam and momentum are conjectures. | Active |
